purpose: Illustrative capability demos, not a benchmark or a general-agent success-rate estimate.
selection_rule: Show the first successful model rollout in the listed order for each category. Retain all attempted rollouts, failures, action distributions and environment outcomes. Scripted mechanics checks are ineligible.
controller: The released checkpoint selects among explicit candidate actions by argmax. No external language model chooses actions. Candidate order is deterministically shuffled.

scope.robot: Native camera image plus simulator state. JevAny selects from eight motion primitives; inverse kinematics and PyBullet execute them. Physical finger contacts hold the cube; no attachment constraint is used.
scope.browser: Actual Chromium on a self-authored local travel sandbox. JevAny receives the screenshot and structured page state, then chooses a visible control. Playwright moves the pointer and clicks. No real travel reservation.
scope.coding: A self-authored Python interval bug. JevAny sees source, failing tests, and four supplied patches, selects one, and the runner applies it and executes pytest. The model does not generate code or shell commands.

success_criteria.robot: Target cube physically inside destination tray, fingers open; other cube remains near its original position.
success_criteria.browser: Actual Chromium page stores the lowest-priced flight satisfying the requested constraints in its local demo itinerary.
success_criteria.coding: Real pytest reproduction fails before the model-selected patch and all twelve cases pass after that exact patch.

presentation.robot_browser: Actual captured environment frames, chronological full action sequence with acceleration, removed inference waits, and outcome hold.
presentation.coding: Visual replay of recorded source, selected diff and actual pytest output. Text reveal is an editing effect, not a real-time terminal recording.
presentation.overlays: Task, selected action, raw option probability and verified environment outcome.

coding-17.goal: Fix adjacent meeting conflicts in half-open intervals.

input_state.goal: Fix the meeting-overlap bug. Intervals use half-open [start, end) semantics, so adjacent meetings are allowed. Choose the patch that preserves genuine overlaps, rejects disjoint/empty intervals, and fixes both adjacency directions.
input_state.source:
"""Half-open meeting intervals, measured in minutes."""


def overlaps(left, right):
    """Return whether two nonempty [start, end) intervals overlap."""
    start_a, end_a = left
    start_b, end_b = right
    if start_a >= end_a or start_b >= end_b:
        return False
    return start_a <= end_b and start_b <= end_a
